land.text: Wiryeseong, where 'Onjo settled ... and called his country Shipje'; Paekche 'initially belonged to the Mahan confederacy'

predecessors.note: Baekje rose inside the Mahan confederacy; the Mahan dossier ends in 346 and hands over its whole Cliopatria shape, which Cliopatria gives to Baekje from 347. The Baekje page puts the founding in 18 BCE; here Baekje is drawn as a small core in the Mahan shape until it takes the rest.

land.text: the Baekje area, for which the 'Tang government set up Ungjin Commandery for the purpose of governing the Paekche area' (Baekje page)

successors.note: 660 to 671; 'Silla drove Tang forces out of most of Baekje's former territory' in 671 (Silla–Tang War page).

land.text: most of the former Baekje, taken from the Tang from 671; Baekje 'ultimately submitted to Unified Silla'

successors.note: The Silla group should decide whether this passes to silla (row to 681) or unified-silla (from 682).

capitals.name: Wiryeseong (Hanam, southern Seoul)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Wirye (18 BCE–475 CE)'; the lead puts Wiryeseong in southern Seoul, the body at 'now Hanam'; the coordinate is Seoul. 'King Gaeru is believed to have moved the capital north of the river to Bukhansanseong in 132.'

capitals.name: Bukhansanseong (north of the Han, Seoul)
capitals.note: 'King Gaeru is believed to have moved the capital north of the river to Bukhansanseong in 132' (Baekje page; ledger capital_move 132). The coordinate is Seoul's, as for the other Seoul-area capitals. Span split by reviewer jk-02-b so the 132 move has its destination in capitals.

capitals.name: Hansan (south-east Seoul)
capitals.note: The Geunchogo page's Samguk Sagi excerpt for 371: the king 'moved our capital to Mt. Hansan', now south-east Seoul; the infobox keeps Wirye to 475. The coordinate is Seoul.

capitals.name: Ungjin (Gongju)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Gomnaru/Ungjin (476–538)'; 'Paekche's capital was located at Ungjin' 475 to 538 in the text.

capitals.name: Sabi (Buyeo)
capitals.note: 'In 538, he moved the capital from Ungjin (present-day Gongju) further south to Sabi (present-day Buyeo County).'

correction.text: the Wiryeseong core of the first Baekje, inside Mahan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -18..233 for the years Cliopatria lacks (its first Baekje shape starts 347 and repeats Mahan's outline). 'Paekche was founded in 18 BCE' by Onjo, who 'settled in Wiryeseong now Hanam'; it 'initially belonged to the Mahan confederacy'. A radius round Seoul is the researcher's reading of the core.

New keyframe 234..346: under Goi (234-286) 'Paekche became a full-fledged kingdom' (Baekje page); the Mahan page: 'Under continuous pressure from Paekche, only 20 statelets of Mahan confederacy survived until the late 3rd century'; the Baekje page: after taking the Han basin it 'overthrew Mokji state'. No page dates the Chungcheong conquests, so Gyeonggi and Chungcheong is the researcher's reading; Jeolla is annexed only in 369 (Geunchogo page).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 347 shape without Jeolla, valid 347..368

keyframe_review.note: The Baekje page gives no area in km2 (only 'approximately 3,800,000 (760,000 households)' and 'controlled most of the western Korean peninsula' at its peak), so the infobox comparison is not possible. Cliopatria's 49,731 km2 for 347..391 is exactly Mahan's outline, handed over whole in 347. The Geunchogo page has 'The remaining tribes of Mahan were annexed in 369, completing Baekje's control over all of present-day Jeolla Province'; so for 347..368 Jeolla is not Baekje's yet.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 347 shape unchanged, for 369..391 (years changed only)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 369..391: the Cliopatria 347 shape as drawn, with Jeolla, from the year the Geunchogo page gives (369). It reaches 38.35N; the page says Baekje took 'the fortress of Pyongyang' in 371 and, undated, controlled 'parts of Gangwon and Hwanghae Provinces'; the outline is kept as drawn.
-1,797 km2 in 392: Gwanggaeto 'attacked Baekje, capturing 10 walled cities' (Gwanggaeto page, 392); Goguryeo's own shape gains the same year.

-4,676 km2 in 395: Baekje 'was pushed south to its capital of Wiryeseong on the Han River'; 396 the capital was taken and Asin 'submitted', but Baekje kept the Han valley until 475 ('in 475, the Seoul region fell to Goguryeo', Baekje page). Goguryeo gains 4,652 km2 in 395.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 476 shape unchanged, valid 476..550 and 553..566 (years changed only)

keyframe_review.note: -8,504 km2 in 476: 'in 475, the Seoul region fell to Goguryeo' (Baekje page), Jangsu 'easily captured the city of Wiryeseong and slew Gaero'; Goguryeo gains 8,404 km2. The shape holds 476..550 and again from 553; for 551..552 Baekje held the Seoul region (next keyframe).

correction.text: the 476 shape plus the Seoul region, Baekje's original capital

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 551..552: 'Baekje regained its original capital in 551' with the aid of Silla and Gaya; 'The campaign culminated in 553 with victories in a series of costly assaults on Goguryeo fortifications', after which Silla 'took possession of the entire Han River valley'. The Seoul region is added to the 476 shape for these two years.

-116 km2 in 567: boundary noise at the Silla edge (Silla gains 11,108 km2 the same year, mostly Gaya). 553: Silla took the Han River valley (Goguryeo page); 554 King Seong was killed at Gwansanseong (Seong page). Shape holds to 655.

Identical outline to 567. 660: 'the coalition troops of Silla and Tang China attacked Paekche' (Baekje page); the Battle of Hwangsanbeol on 9 July 660; the capital Sabi 'fell almost immediately thereafter' and King Uija was sent into exile in China.

ledger.note: 18 BCE: Onjo founds Baekje at Wiryeseong. 'Paekche was founded in 18 BCE' by Onjo; 'Onjo settled in Wiryeseong now Hanam, and called his country Shipje'; the lead puts Wiryeseong in southern Seoul. It 'initially belonged to the Mahan confederacy'.
132: King Gaeru is believed to have moved the capital north of the river to Bukhansanseong ('believed' on the page).

From 234, Baekje spreads over Gyeonggi and Chungcheong. Goi (234-286): 'Paekche became a full-fledged kingdom' (Baekje page); Mahan page: 'only 20 statelets of Mahan confederacy survived until the late 3rd century'. The pages give no conquest dates; 234 is a bridging date.
369: Geunchogo annexes the last of Mahan. 'The remaining tribes of Mahan were annexed in 369, completing Baekje's control over all of present-day Jeolla Province.'
371: Geunchogo moves the capital to Mt. Hansan (south-east Seoul), the year his army under Crown Prince Geungusu 'took the fortress of Pyongyang and killed Gogugwon of Goguryeo'.

region.text: the ten walled cities taken in 392

ledger.note: 392: Gwanggaeto takes ten Baekje walled cities. He attacked Baekje with 40,000 troops, 'capturing 10 walled cities'; the page names none, so the region is the land Baekje's Cliopatria shape loses in 392.

region.text: the Han River heartland round Wiryeseong

ledger.note: 392-396: the war for the Han River heartland. 393 and 394 Asin 'was defeated' twice; 395 Baekje 'was pushed south to its capital of Wiryeseong'.
395: Baekje is pushed back to Wiryeseong ('was pushed south to its capital of Wiryeseong on the Han River').

region.text: the Han River heartland round Wiryeseong

ledger.note: 396: Gwanggaeto captures the Baekje capital and Asin 'submitted to him', surrendering 'a prince and 10 government ministers'; the Han valley stays Baekje's until 475.

region.text: the Seoul region and Han River valley

ledger.note: 475: Goguryeo takes Wiryeseong. 'Jangsu easily captured the city of Wiryeseong and slew Gaero' and burned the capital; Baekje moved to Ungjin, 'more or less total control of the Han River valley' went to Goguryeo (Baekje page: 'in 475, the Seoul region fell to Goguryeo').
475: the capital moves to Ungjin (Gongju): 'Paekche's capital was located at Ungjin' 475 to 538; infobox 476.

region.text: Jeju Island, the kingdom of Tamna

ledger.note: 476: Tamna becomes Baekje's tributary. 'In 476, according to the Samguk Sagi, Tamna entered into a tributary relationship with Baekje'; the infobox says 'Tributary state of Baekje (498–660)'.
538: King Seong moves the capital to Sabi. 'In 538, he moved the capital from Ungjin (present-day Gongju) further south to Sabi (present-day Buyeo County).'
After 538 the state calls itself Nambuyeo (Southern Buyeo). 'He changed the name of the country to Nambuyeo.' The page gives no year; 538 is a bridging date. Colour and dossier continue.

region.text: the Seoul region, Baekje's original capital

ledger.note: 551: Baekje retakes its old capital. 'Baekje regained its original capital in 551', with the aid of Silla and the Gaya confederacy.
551: Baekje and Silla 'entered into an alliance to attack Goguryeo'; the Han River valley is fought over until 553.

553: Silla takes the Han River valley. 'Silla took possession of the entire Han River valley in 553' (Goguryeo page); the Seong page has it after the 553 campaign and before the following year's retaliatory strike. The pages do not say whether Silla took it from Baekje or Goguryeo, so Baekje's loss is the Seoul region it regained in 551.
553: the Han River valley is Silla's. 554: Seong 'and 30,000 Baekje troops were killed in the disastrous battle' at Gwansanseong.

region.text: Jeju Island, the kingdom of Tamna

ledger.note: 660: the Baekje tributary relation ends with the fall of Baekje (infobox 'Tributary state of Baekje (498–660)').

660: Silla and Tang end Baekje. 'In 660, the coalition troops of Silla and Tang China attacked Paekche' (Baekje page); the Battle of Hwangsanbeol, 9 July 660, Kim Yu-sin's 50,000 against General Gyebaek; 'Baekje soon fell when Kim Yu-Sin and the Tang general Su Dingfang surrounded Gongju and King Uija surrendered'. The Tang 'set up Ungjin Commandery'; the revival under Buyeo Pung was crushed at Baekgang in August 663.

wars.name: Baekje–Goguryeo war of 369-371
wars.outcome: Baekje repelled Goguryeo at Chiyang in 369; in 371 its army of 30,000 'took the fortress of Pyongyang and killed Gogugwon of Goguryeo'. No border changed.

wars.name: Gwanggaeto's conquest of Baekje
wars.outcome: Goguryeo took ten walled cities in 392 and more land in 395; in 396 it captured the capital and Asin submitted.

wars.name: Goguryeo's conquest of Hanseong
wars.outcome: Jangsu captured Wiryeseong and killed King Gaero; Baekje moved to Ungjin.

wars.name: Baekje–Silla campaign against Goguryeo
wars.outcome: Baekje regained its old capital in 551; in 553 Silla took the Han River valley; King Seong was killed at Gwansanseong in 554.
wars.note: The Seong page does not give a year for the Silla seizure; the Goguryeo page has 553.

wars.name: Silla–Tang conquest of Baekje
wars.outcome: Kim Yu-sin's Silla army won at Hwangsanbeol on 9 July 660 and, with Su Dingfang's Tang army, took the Baekje capital; King Uija surrendered and went into exile in China.

wars.name: Baekje restoration and Baekgang
wars.outcome: Dochim and Buyeo Boksin brought Buyeo Pung back from Japan with 10,000 soldiers; the Silla–Tang forces won the naval battles at Baekgang in August 663 and Pung escaped to Goguryeo.
wars.note: Cliopatria draws nothing after 660; the dossier ends in 660 because the page calls the movement 'a brief restoration movement'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is recorded. The Han River frontier with Goguryeo and Silla moved with each campaign (392-396, 475, 551-553) and is drawn soft throughout; the southern coast is not a political frontier.

notes:
Cliopatria's Baekje row (347..660, six shapes) starts with Mahan's exact outline, 49,731 km2, in the year Mahan ends. The Baekje page puts the founding in 18 BCE inside the Mahan confederacy, so the dossier starts at -18 and adds two new keyframes for -18..233 (a Seoul core) and 234..346 (Gyeonggi and Chungcheong, a reading: no page dates the Chungcheong conquests). The Mahan dossier (jk-02-a) draws the whole Mahan shape to 346, so the two overlap on the Baekje core until then; the renderer should let Baekje win.
Jeolla is only Baekje's from 369 (Geunchogo page); the 347 shape is therefore adjusted (minus Jeolla) for 347..368, and the unchanged shape is a new keyframe 369..391.
The Baekje page's 'may have even held territories in China, such as in the Liaoxi Commandery' is called controversial and is not drawn; 'as far north as Pyongyang' at the 4th-century peak rests only on the 371 capture of the Pyongyang fortress and is not drawn either (Cliopatria's shape stops at 38.35N).
Tributaries: Tamna 476 (page) or 498 (infobox) to 660; Gaya states west of the Nakdong became Baekje dependencies, undated (Geunchogo page) and the Nihon Shoki 249 claim are not drawn; the Gaya dossier should carry any vassal relation.
After 660 the Tang Ungjin Commandery (660 to 671) and Silla's 671 recovery belong to the Tang and Silla dossiers; Buyeo Pung's revival to August 663 (Baekgang) is a war here only.
Counterparts to be mirrored: Goguryeo (392-396 contest, 475, 551-553), Silla (553; Tang 660-671), Tamna (Silla's later tribute 662 etc.).
Pages that gave nothing for Baekje's budget: none beyond the missing month of Sabi's fall (Hwangsanbeol page: no month). No rulers listed: the Baekje page has a king table that was not read.
Note: Cliopatria 567 shape is 116 km2 smaller than 476; the pages give no Baekje–Silla frontier event in 567.
